heroHeadline: China Leads Launch of World's First International Solid-State Battery Standard
heroSubtitle: The week of August 19–26, 2026 brought a wave of battery-storage and next-gen chemistry milestones. China's SAMR secured IEC approval on August 21 to lead the world's first international testing standard for solid-state EV batteries, with France, Japan, and South Korea participating. Saudi Arabia's SPPC awarded $1.16 billion in build-own-operate contracts for 2 GW/8 GWh of standalone battery storage on August 20 — the Kingdom's first tender of its kind — while US utility-scale battery storage neared 52 GW as of June 2026, growing roughly 70% annually per EIA data. BYD launched its Da Han flagship sedan on August 22 with a second-generation Blade Battery supporting 10-70% flash charging in 5 minutes and 1,008 km CLTC range. Critical Metals Corp amended its takeover structure for European Lithium's Wolfsberg project — Europe's first fully permitted lithium mine — targeting a September close. Lithium carbonate prices, after sliding to an August 12 low near $18,310/tonne, jumped 5.39% in a single session on August 24 to roughly $24,086/tonne on surging energy-storage demand.
footerNote: Data sourced from official company reports, IEA, BloombergNEF, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, SNE Research, pv magazine, and peer-reviewed publications. Lab results distinguished from commercial production figures throughout.
